text:
A bead of mass ' $m$ ' slides without friction on the wall of a vertical circular hoop of radius ' $R$ ' as shown in figure. The bead moves under the combined action of gravity and a massless spring (k) attached to the bottom of the hoop. The equilibrium length of the spring is ' $R$ '. If the bead is released from top of the hoop with (negligible) zero initial speed, velocity of bead, when the length of spring becomes ' $R$ ', would be (spring constant is ' $k$ ', $g$ is acceleration due to gravity)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The spring joins the lowest point $O$ of the hoop to the bead. At the top, the spring length is $2R$, so its extension is $2R-R=R$, and the bead is at height $2R$ above $O$.

When the spring length becomes $R$, the centre $C$, the lowest point $O$ and the bead $B$ form a triangle with $CO=CB=OB=R$, which is equilateral. So $OB$ makes $60^{\circ }$ with the vertical $OC$, and the height of $B$ above $O$ is

$h_{2}=R\cos 60^{\circ }=\dfrac{R}{2}$


[IMG]

At this position the spring is at its natural (equilibrium) length, so it stores no energy. The hoop is frictionless and the normal force does no work, so mechanical energy is conserved:

$\dfrac{1}{2}kR^{2}+mg(2R)=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}+mg\dfrac{R}{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}kR^{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}mgR\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{3Rg+\dfrac{kR^{2}}{m}}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

Assertion A: A sound wave has higher speed in solids than gases.

Reason R: Gases have higher value of Bulk modulus than solids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true and $𝐑$ is the correct explanation of $𝐀$
Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true but $𝐑$ is NOT the correct explanation of $𝐀$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, speed of sound in a medium $v=\sqrt{\frac{B}{ρ}}$ where B = bulk modulus, $ρ$ = density of the medium

Since, solids and liquids are much more difficult to compress than gases so they have much higher values of bulk modulus.

i.e., $B_{solid}>B_{liquid}>B_{gas}$

Generally solids and liquids have higher mass densities ($ρ$) than gases. But corresponding increase in bulk modulus is much higher.

So, $v_{solid}>v_{liquid}>v_{gas}$

Hence, option C is correct.

text:
In the experiment for measurement of viscosity ' $η$ ' of given liquid with a ball having radius $R$, consider following statements.

A. Graph between terminal velocity V and R will be a parabola.

B. The terminal velocities of different diameter balls are constant for a given liquid.

C. Measurement of terminal velocity is dependent on the temperature.

D. This experiment can be utilized to assess the density of a given liquid.

E. If balls are dropped with some initial speed, the value of $η$ will change.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, terminal velocity of a sphere of radius R in a liquid of viscosity $η$,

$v=\frac{2}{9}\frac{R^{2}g}{η}(σ-ρ)$ .... (1)

where, $σ$ = mass density of sphere

$ρ$ = density of liquid

we can see, $v\propto R^{2}$ (for constant $η,σ$ & $ρ$)

Hence, graph between v and R is parabola.

As v depends on R so the terminal velocities of different diameter balls will be different.
We know, the viscosity of a liquid usually decreases as the temperature increases and $v\propto \frac{1}{η}$

So terminal velocity depends on the temperature. $T↑\Rightarrow η↓\Rightarrow v↑$

As the equation $v=\frac{2}{9}\frac{R^{2}g}{η}(σ-ρ)$ involves density of liquid $ρ$. So the experiment can be utilized to assess it.

From (1), $η=\frac{2}{9}\frac{R^{2}g}{v}(σ-ρ)$

Here, $η$ does not depend on initial speed of the sphere. Hence, option 3 is correct.

text:
The center of mass of a thin rectangular plate (fig - x ) with sides of length $a$ and $b$, whose mass per unit area $(σ)$ varies as $σ=\frac{σ_{0}x}{ab}$ (where $σ_{0}$ is a constant), would be $__________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$σ=\frac{σ_{0}x}{ab}$

Let's consider a strip of infinitesimal width dx at x distance away from O.

As $σ$ depends only on x i.e. it's constant for a specific value of x so centre of mass of the strip will be $\left (x,\frac{b}{2}\right )$.

Now, we know,

$COM=\left (\frac{\int xdm}{\int dm},\frac{\int ydm}{\int dm}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{\int xσdA}{\int σdA},\frac{\int \frac{b}{2}σdA}{\int σdA}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{\int xbdx\frac{σ0x}{ab}}{\int \frac{σ0x}{ab}bdx},\frac{\frac{b}{2}\int σdA}{\int σdA}\right )$

For whole plate, x varies from o to a.

So, $COM=\left (\frac{\frac{σ0}{a}\int _{0}^{a}x^{2}dx}{\frac{σ0}{a}\int _{0}^{a}xdx},\frac{b}{2}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{\frac{1}{3}\left [x^{3}\right ]_{0}^{a}}{\frac{1}{2}[x^{2}]_{0}^{a}},\frac{b}{2}\right )$

$=\left (\frac{2}{3}\frac{a^{3}}{a^{2}},\frac{b}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow COM=\left (\frac{2}{3}a,\frac{b}{2}\right )$

text:
Consider following statements:

A. Surface tension arises due to extra energy of the molecules at the interior as compared to the molecules at the surface, of a liquid.

B. As the temperature of liquid rises, the coefficient of viscosity increases.

C. As the temperature of gas increases, the coefficient of viscosity increases

D. The onset of turbulence is determined by Reynold's number.

E. In a steady flow two stream lines never intersect.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A is false: molecules at the surface have fewer neighbours and carry extra potential energy compared with molecules in the interior; surface tension arises from this extra energy of the surface molecules.

Statement B is false: the viscosity of a liquid decreases as its temperature rises, because the intermolecular attraction between layers weakens.

Statement C is true: the viscosity of a gas increases with temperature, because faster molecules carry more momentum between neighbouring layers.

Statement D is true: the Reynolds number $R_{e}=\dfrac{ρvD}{η}$ decides the onset of turbulence; the flow is laminar at small $R_{e}$ and becomes turbulent above a critical value.

Statement E is true: the tangent to a streamline gives the direction of the fluid velocity at that point; in steady flow a point has a single velocity, so two streamlines can never intersect.

The correct statements are C, D and E.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: A proton of mass ' $m_{P}$ ' has same energy ' $E$ ' as that of a photon of wavelength ' $λ$ '. If the proton is moving at non-relativistic speed, then ratio of its de Broglie wavelength to the wavelength of photon is.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of a proton to the wavelength of a photon when they have the same energy, we follow these steps:

Energy Equivalence:  

Both the proton and the photon have the same energy, denoted by E.

Energy of the Photon:  

The energy of a photon with wavelength λ is given by:  

$E=\frac{hc}{λ}$

Kinetic Energy of the Proton:  

Since the proton moves at a non-relativistic speed, its kinetic energy can be expressed as:  

$\text{KE}_{\text{proton}}=\frac{1}{2}m_{P}v^{2}=E$

Momentum of the Proton:  

The momentum p of the proton is derived from its kinetic energy:  

$p=\sqrt{2m_{P}E}$

de Broglie Wavelength of the Proton:  

The de Broglie wavelength $λ_{$proton} is:  

$λ_{\text{proton}}=\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_{P}E}}$

Ratio of Wavelengths:  

The ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the proton to the wavelength of the photon is:  

$\frac{λ_{\text{proton}}}{λ_{\text{photon}}}=\left (\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_{P}E}}\right )\times \left (\frac{E}{hc}\right )$  

Simplifying, we get:  

$\frac{λ_{\text{proton}}}{λ_{\text{photon}}}=\frac{1}{c}\sqrt{\frac{E}{2m_{P}}}$

Thus, the ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the proton to the wavelength of the photon is $\frac{1}{c}\sqrt{\frac{E}{2m_{P}}}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: Consider a long thin conducting wire carrying a uniform current I. A particle having mass " $m$ " and charge " $q$ " is released at a distance " $a$ " from the wire with a speed $v_{0}$ along the direction of current in the wire. The particle gets attracted to the wire due to magnetic force. The particle turns round when it is at distance $x$ from the wire. The value of $x$ is [ $μ_{0}$ is vacuum permeability]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take the wire along the $y$-axis with the current in the $+y$ direction, and the particle at $x=a$ with velocity $v_{0}\hat{j}$. At distance $x$ the field is $⃗{B}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2πx}(-\hat{k})$.

The magnetic force does no work, so the speed remains $v_{0}$ throughout.

The $y$-component of $⃗{F}=q⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}$ is $qv_{x}B$, so

$m\frac{dv_{y}}{dt}=\frac{qμ_{0}I}{2πx}\frac{dx}{dt}\Rightarrow mdv_{y}=\frac{qμ_{0}I}{2π}\frac{dx}{x}$

At the turning point $v_{x}=0$; since the speed is $v_{0}$ and $v_{y}$ has decreased from $v_{0}$ (as $x<a$), there $v_{y}=-v_{0}$.

Integrating from $(x=a,v_{y}=v_{0})$ to $(x,v_{y}=-v_{0})$:

$m(-v_{0}-v_{0})=\frac{qμ_{0}I}{2π}\ln \frac{x}{a}\Rightarrow \ln \frac{x}{a}=-\frac{4πmv_{0}}{qμ_{0}I}$

$x=ae^{-\frac{4πmv0}{qμ0I}}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: Three infinitely long wires with linear charge density $λ$ are placed along the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Which of the following denotes an equipotential surface?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The field of an infinitely long line charge $λ$ at perpendicular distance $r$ is $E=\dfrac{2kλ}{r}$, directed radially outward, with $k=\dfrac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}$. Its potential is therefore

$V=-\int Edr=-2kλ\ln r+C$

A point $(x,y,z)$ is at perpendicular distance $\sqrt{y^{2}+z^{2}}$ from the $x$-axis, $\sqrt{z^{2}+x^{2}}$ from the $y$-axis and $\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}$ from the $z$-axis.

Adding the potentials of the three wires,

$V=-2kλ\left [\ln \sqrt{y^{2}+z^{2}}+\ln \sqrt{z^{2}+x^{2}}+\ln \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right ]+C=-kλ\ln \left [(x^{2}+y^{2})(y^{2}+z^{2})(z^{2}+x^{2})\right ]+C$

$V$ is constant exactly when $(x^{2}+y^{2})(y^{2}+z^{2})(z^{2}+x^{2})$ is constant, so this is the equipotential surface.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: Two iron solid discs of negligible thickness have radii $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ and moment of inertia $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$, respectively. For $R_{2}=2R_{1}$, the ratio of $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ would be $1/x$, where $\mathrm{x}=$ $_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let surface mass density = $σ$

So, $M_{1}=σ\times πR_{1}^{2}$

$M_{2}=σ\times πR_{2}^{2}=σπ(2R_{1})^{2}$ (As $R_{2}=2R_{1}$)

$=4σπR_{1}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow M_{2}=4M_{1}$

$\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\frac{\frac{M1R2 1}{2}}{\frac{M2R2 2}{2}}=\left (\frac{M_{1}}{M_{2}}\right )\left (\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\left (\frac{M_{1}}{4M_{1}}\right )\left (\frac{R_{1}}{2R_{1}}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{4}\times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{16}=\frac{1}{x}$

Hence, $x=16$

text: In a measurement, it is asked to find modulus of elasticity per unit torque applied on the system. The measured quantity has dimension of $\left [M^{a}L^{b}T^{c}\right ]$. If $b=-3$, the value of $c$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, measured quantity $=\frac{Modulusofelasticity}{torque}$

$=\frac{σ}{ετ}=\frac{F}{Aετ}$ where, $σ$ = stress, $ε$ = strain, $τ$ = torque

$=\frac{F}{AεFL}$

So, dimension $=\frac{1}{[L^{2}][L]}$ ($ε$ is dimensionless)

$=[L^{-3}]=[M^{0}L^{-3}T^{0}]=[M^{a}L^{b}T^{c}]$

$\Rightarrow c=0$

text: A tiny metallic rectangular sheet has length and breadth of 5 mm and 2.5 mm , respectively. Using a specially designed screw gauge which has pitch of 0.75 mm and 15 divisions in the circular scale, you are asked to find the area of the sheet. In this measurement, the maximum fractional error will be $\frac{x}{100}$ where $x$ is $_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Given, L = 5 mm, B = 2.5 mm

We know, least count of a screw gauge,

$L.C.=\frac{\text{Pitch length}}{\text{No. of division on circular scale}}$

$\Rightarrow L.C.=\frac{0.75}{15}=0.05mm$

We know, $A=LB$

By taking $\ln $ on both sides,

$\Rightarrow \ln A=\ln L+\ln B$

by differentiating both sides,

$\Rightarrow \frac{dA}{A}=\frac{dL}{L}+\frac{dB}{B}$

Here, $dL=dB=0.05mm$ (L.C.)

So fractional error,

$\frac{dA}{A}=\frac{0.05}{5}+\frac{0.05}{2.5}$

$=\frac{1}{100}+\frac{2}{100}=\frac{3}{100}=\frac{x}{100}$ (given)

Hence, $x=3$.

text: A double slit interference experiment performed with a light of wavelength 600 nm forms an interference fringe pattern on a screen with 10 th bright fringe having its centre at a distance of 10 mm from the central maximum. Distance of the centre of the same 10 th bright fringe from the central maximum when the source of light is replaced by another source of wavelength 660 nm would be $________ mm$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Young's double slit experiment, the distance of $n^{th}$ maxima from central maxima is given by,

$Y=\frac{nλD}{d}$

Here, $n,D$ & $d$ are same for both the cases.

So, $Y\propto λ$

$\Rightarrow \frac{Y_{1}}{Y_{2}}=\frac{λ_{1}}{λ_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{10}{Y_{2}}=\frac{600}{660}=\frac{10}{11}$

$\Rightarrow Y_{2}=11mm$.
